summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of systolic heart failure (LVEF ≤30%), ischemic cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and obesity, was admitted for worsening chest pressure, shortness of breath, and an ICD shock due to symptomatic ventricular tachycardia. He was found to be fluid overloaded, with bilateral crackles, elevated proBNP, and pulmonary edema on imaging. He was treated with IV diuresis, which improved his volume status, and started on a lidocaine drip and amiodarone for VT suppression. An attempted VT ablation was unsuccessful due to inability to induce the arrhythmia during electrophysiology study. His digoxin dose was reduced due to amiodarone interaction. He stabilized with improved symptoms and was discharged on amiodarone, adjusted digoxin, and home heart failure medications, with follow-up planned for lab monitoring and cardiology evaluation.
